reserveReview.rationale: KMS Labs states each ERC-20 KAU is backed 1:1 by Kinesis-native KAU held in segregated wallets maintained by KMS Labs; native KAU's allocated physical-gold backing is a second-layer asset and not the ERC-20 token's direct reserve. Coverage scope measured 2026-09-11: the Chainlink PoR feed's answer (2,567,133.466 with 18 decimals) is the audited Kinesis Cayman fine-gold balance, and the issuer reconciles that balance against Kinesis-native KAU circulation (2,565,133.465 at audit ledger 43137668 on 2026-04-20; 3,987,303.5292 at ledger 45450621 on 2026-09-10), not against any single-chain token supply. The only registry-readable KAU deployment is the Ethereum ERC-20 wrapper 0x14dab79fd7b7b3f748d434812fd6a9aac460ea52 (1,640,000 totalSupply at 2026-09-11, 88.96% of it in one address), which the bridge review and mint-authority review both classify as a KMS Labs representation of native KAU. That wrapper supply is therefore a subset of the native-chain liability the feed covers, so comparing the two produced the artefactual 156.53% over-coverage; the live config declares `incompleteSupplyScope` and publishes no ratio.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: KMS Labs administers the segregated native-KAU reserve wallet linked on its website. The October 1, 2026 Kinesis account response lists four ed25519 signers of weight 3, a master-key weight of 0, and medium/high thresholds of 5; spending therefore requires at least two listed signers under the reported threshold configuration. Signer identity, independence, and MPC/HSM custody are not disclosed. Its terms expressly deny ERC-20 holders legal, equitable, or beneficial title to reserves and a trust or fiduciary relationship. ABX, Brinks, and Loomis describe underlying native-KAU bullion custody only. Independent ERC-20 reserve verification, statutory bankruptcy remoteness, and a rehypothecation prohibition are not established.
